**P-POSSUM** is a postoperative risk scoring system that relies on pre-operative and intra-operative observations to assess patient outcomes. Within the context of the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) and the broader national quality development efforts led by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), P-POSSUM is evaluated alongside other risk stratification models such as [[apache|APACHE]], ASA, Charlson, and Surgical Apgar. The core challenge highlighted in the AKDB reports is the inherent tension between evidence-based medicine and the practical implementability of these complex tools in everyday clinical routines.

Despite its clinical relevance, the AKDB steering committee has assessed P-POSSUM to be too comprehensive and burdensome for practical, daily use [^src1]. This methodological assessment was specifically noted in discussions surrounding alternative scoring systems for [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] [^src1]. Similarly, in the evaluation of [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which focuses on the intermediate admission of high-risk patients, P-POSSUM and APACHE were both deemed too extensive for practical implementation [^src2]. Ultimately, the database prioritizes simpler, more easily integrated metrics over complex scoring systems that might hinder routine data collection.
